data.name: Ben
data.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Ben means 'son' and 'of the south'. It is a biblical name derived from the Hebrew word ben, which means 'son' in the Hebrew language. The name Ben is often associated with the son of Jacob, named Ben-onni, which means 'son of my pain' or 'son of my sorrow'.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes God's love and compassion towards his children

in_hebrew.name: בן
in_hebrew.meaning: בנו של הבן בכור אלוקים משמעותו בן האל הבכור
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם בן הוא שורש עברי שמשמעותו בן או בנו של. הוא קשור קשר הדוק למילה העברית בן, שפירושה בן או צאצא. בהקשר של שמות נוצריים, בן הוא לעתים קרובות קיצור של שמות כמו בנימין או אברהם בן. השם בן מופיע בתנ"ך כבן של אלוקים, בן של אדם, וכינוי לאישיות רוחנית. הוא נושא משמעות עמוקה של קשר משפחתי ורוחני כאחד.

in_greek.name: Μπεν
in_greek.meaning: Ο Μπεν ως όνομα σημαίνει υιός ή παιδί
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μπεν, προερχόμενο από την εβραϊκή ρίζα, έχει υιοθετηθεί και στην ελληνική χριστιανική παράδοση. Στη Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοια ονόματα όπως Βενιαμίν (Βeniamin) αναφέρονται. Το Μπεν ως ανεξάρτητο όνομα φέρει τη σημασία του υιού ή του παιδιού, συμβολίζοντας στενή σχέση με το Θεό ή πνευματική πατρότητα.

in_latin.name: Ben
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ben ex hebraeo origine derivatum est, et in traditione christiana latina interpretatur ut filius benedictus. Cum primitivum nomen ebraicum sit בן (Ben), id significat filium vel puellam. In ecclesia christiana, nomen Ben saepe ut abbreviationem nominum hebraeorum antiquorum ut Beniamin assumitur. Simbolizat relationem filiationis divinae et spiritualis.

in_english.name: Ben
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ben originates from the Hebrew root בן (ben), meaning 'son' or 'young one.' It is commonly used as a short form of names like Benjamin or Benedict. In Christian tradition, Ben symbolizes divine sonship and spiritual inheritance. Historically, it has been used across various Christian cultures, embodying virtues of filial piety and divine blessing.

biblical_reference.note: Ben is referenced as part of Hebrew names in the Old Testament.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ben is a commonly used name among Christians, especially in the United States, and it has strong cultural roots. The name has been in use since biblical times and continues to be a popular choice for parents looking for a meaningful name for their child. It is a name that signifies sonship, lineage, and a connection to the past.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, the name Ben carries deep significance as it reminds us of our spiritual sonship with God. Just as a physical son is born from his father's seed, we too are spiritual sons and daughters of God, born of His love and grace. The name Ben can serve as a reminder to live in accordance with our divine sonship, to honor and serve our Father in heaven, and to strive for holiness and righteousness in our lives. Additionally, the association of the name Ben with the southern region may also hold spiritual significance, as some interpretations of the Bible view the south as a symbol of spiritual protection and refuge.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Benedict of Nursia (480-543 AD) was an Italian monk and the founder of the Benedictine Order. The name Ben carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

trends: Common name in the United States, United Kingdom, and other English-speaking countries
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ben remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
